transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I'm here today because I've been really struggling to stay focused and pay attention to my work and daily tasks lately. It feels like I just can't sustain my focus on any single thing for more than a few minutes.
Has this difficulty with focus been a lifelong struggle for you, or is this a more recent change that has developed over the last few months?

It has gotten significantly worse over the last nine months, but it is actually a long-standing issue for me. I can remember struggling with my focus all the way back in elementary school, definitely before I was 12. It has just become much harder to manage recently.
Beyond difficulty with focus, do you often find yourself feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

Yes, I definitely experience that. I often feel very restless inside and have a really hard time sitting still for long. Because of that, I find myself constantly fidgeting, tapping my hands or feet, or squirming in my seat.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a long-standing history of both inattentive symptoms (starting before age 12) and clear, persistent hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, fidgeting). Given the presence of both domains, ADHD (Combined Presentation) is the most accurate diagnosis among the candidates.
